steps.content: In the interrogation room, Corso sits slumped in a chair, her chin resting in her hand. She looks sideways at you when you come in. Despite her relaxed posture, the intensity of her gaze is unmistakable.
Corso is warlike. She was arrested by the sheriffs during a low-level fighting contest and then transferred to the MBCC.

The reasons given by the FAC for her arrest are "picking quarrels and provoking trouble," "disrupting public order," "compromising the fairness of the contest," and "revealing her identity as a Sinner."
You met Corso on several occasions when she was still a member of Rustfire. You don't know her well, but her unconventional behavior has made a strong impression on you.
This Sinner is fickle and unpredictable like a ticking time bomb. It's wise to be on your guard around her, even though you have put the shackles on her.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Ah, it's you... What am I here for? Just come right out and tell me.
It's about a disciplinary issue.
test
test
test
test
test
test
I've received a report on your performance regarding the recent field operation.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Oh, what does it say?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Does it mention how flawless my combat skills are, or how beautifully I accomplished my tasks?
Corso bursts into laughter. A realization, though an incorrect one, has come to her.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: You brought me here, to compliment me?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Hahaha... You guys are discerning, I'll give you that.
Corso's unabashed self-praise renders you speechless for a moment.
Don't flatter yourself.
According to the report, you disobeyed orders and went AWOL without explanation, and this happened on multiple occasions.
This is a serious disciplinary violation for a Sinner. Explain yourself!

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Geez, this is what I'm here for?
Corso yawns, bored again.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: My reason for going AWOL... Well, let's just say I felt like it, all right?
Take this seriously, and answer my question!
In the heat of the moment, you smack your hand, along with the report, down on the table. You then point out the glaring section where her misconduct is listed.
You absconded to do what? Answer me!

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Okay, okay... Good Lord, you're a real pain in the neck.
Corso picks up the report and gives it a once-over before releasing it and blowing it away.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Those few days I went missing, I fought in some fighting contests. I can't believe you're pestering me with this tiny-ass thing.
Fighting contests?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Yeah.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: The tasks you assigned me were too easy; they were just warm-up exercises. And those obedient Sinners of yours, none of them wanted to fight me. It was killing me, the boredom.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: So I took matters into my own hands and went looking for some action.
As Corso explains her disappearances, the accusatory tone is hard to miss, as if the MBCC had mistreated her in some way.
Your reason sounds far-fetched to me.
You call up a map of Syndicate and circle a few spots on the map.
I've put the shackles on you, so I know where you've been to.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I'm aware of that. I went to these places, because that's where most fighting contests are held these days.
Corso remains nonchalant. You frown.
These are some of the most dangerous places in Syndicate. If I'm not mistaken, it's in one of these places that you were arrested.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: So what?
I want you to be honest with me.
Besides taking part in fighting contests, did you do something else after you snuck away?
Corso straightens up slightly and raises her eyebrows at you.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Something else? Please, enlighten me, what else could I have done? Because I don't have a clue.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
Following the Rustfire infighting, most of its grassroots members left the organization. They're now scattered around Syndicate.
They're under the influence of Mania, so they are mentally unstable, and highly liable to mental derangement when incited. They have already caused many outbreaks of public disorder.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Why are you telling me this? I can't see how it has anything to do with me.
You scrutinize Corso's smiling face, but it gives nothing away.
We have reason to believe that you might have gotten in touch with some of the former Rustfire members.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: What? You're so hilarious.
Corso guffaws, as if you've just told the funniest joke in the world.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Hahaha... You're not seriously thinking that I'm the one who incited them to cause trouble?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: My "brilliant" Chief, you have been misled by your preconceptions.
Under your scathing gaze, Corso finally stops laughing and resumes talking.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I did work with those brainless guys occasionally when I was still a member. But I'm nothing like them.
Then how do you explain why they always showed up in the same places as you?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Well, these old "friends" of mine, they are drawn to things that are exciting and violent.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: And fighting contests are exciting and violent.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: To tell you the truth, some of them did come up to me at one time or another, but I just gave them the cold shoulder. I'd rather have a couple more fights than listen to their nonsense.
Why do I get the feeling that you don't like them very much?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I loathe them. Like I said, I'm nothing like them.
Then why did you join Rustfire in the first place?
Corso laughs, more loudly this time.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Rustfire meant nothing to me.
She shrugs, almost dramatically, her face wearing a scornful look.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I joined them, simply because it gave me a chance to challenge the great fighters in the organization.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Rustfire was just a source of entertainment for me. I couldn't care less about their game plan.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: They talked about rejuvenating Syndicate, about protecting the downtrodden. That only made me laugh.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: The truth is that they were just a bunch of scum. Their ego was magnified by the little power they possessed, and their judgment was clouded as a result.
Corso shakes her head, putting on a hurt expression, while her tone is dripping with contempt.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Intimidation, violence, robbery, looting... They were capable of anything. They were not much different from those who they vowed to take down.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I was sick of them, those brainless predators. So I returned to my old pastime; fighting contests are good fun.
When the subject returns to fighting contests, Corso becomes animated. She leans forward and starts speaking in an excited tone.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: You won't believe how thrilling it is to beat one fighter after another!

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I'm reaching the top. But there is this one fighter I haven't beaten yet. When I defeat him, I'll become the best fighter there is.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: To tell you the truth, I snuck away to look for him, the man who stands between me and the Holy Grail.
You were looking for a man?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Yes. A man I have yet to defeat.
Corso pauses for a moment, then speaks again through gritted teeth.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: I must defeat him to attain the ultimate glory in the underground arena.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: But he looks down on me and sees our matches as a chore. Sometimes, he just disappears right before our match starts, nowhere to be seen.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: He makes a fascinating opponent, more fascinating even than the great fighters in Rustfire. I'm taking part in every fighting contest I can find in Syndicate, because I want to find him and defeat him once and for all.
You can see the fierce determination in her eyes, and it is also clearly conveyed to you through the shackles. You know for sure that she is not lying.
That's no excuse for disciplinary violations.
You're now one of the Sinners managed by the MBCC. You're working under me; I'm responsible for you, both in terms of your behavior and your work.
I'll take your situation into consideration. In the future, I'll assign more challenging tasks to you, to satisfy your need for, um, exercise.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Ah, that's fantastic. I like challenging tasks. The more, the better.
Corso is elated, but her elation is curtailed by your attaching a condition, delivered in a measured tone, to the arrangement.
But at the same time, you need to agree to closer supervision.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Closer supervision?
Yes. Someone will stay by your side around the clock whenever you're out for a task, to make sure you won't fly the coop again.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: ${PlayerName}... Chief, what about this?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: You can give me as many tasks as I can manage, and I promise I'll carry them out to the best of my ability. There's really no need to have someone watch over me...
She is trying to negotiate with you, but her voice sounds somewhat threatening.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Look, I've completed so many tasks for you without asking for anything in return. How about you give me some of those... what do they call it, uh, yes, Sinner benefits?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Please don't take away my freedom. I need to be able to go around and enjoy my pastime.
Your pastime? You mean fighting contests?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: What else could it be? Didn't I make myself clear enough?
Corso haggles on with dogged persistence. You can't help but snort with laughter.
You were very clear. Still, I can't let you run around like a wild animal. We have rules here in the MBCC. We can't break them just for someone's convenience.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: All right then. If that's the case, how about we host a fighting contest here in the MBCC?
What?

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Well, some of your Sinners seem like strong fighters. I challenged them to a fight before, but none was on board. Could you get them to accept my challenge?
Corso's voice is getting more excited, and her eyes are growing brighter, like those of a predator ready to pounce on its prey.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Or maybe you can be my opponent. What do you say? I've been wondering about that curious ability of yours, the one you use to restrain me.
She leans even closer. And you lean back to keep a comfortable distance between you.
I can answer your questions now...
My answers are... no and no.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Why?
Corso, I respect your inclinations and needs, and I'm trying my best to accommodate them.
You can't be a lone wolf, that's the bottom line. If you keep pushing it, you won't get any preferential treatment from me.
And you won't be allowed to go on field operations anymore.
In the face of your tough stand, the playful smile Corso has been wearing like a mask starts to dissolve. She stares at you with a frown on her face, and you stare back.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: All right, all right, I'll take the deal.
Corso reclines back on the chair, nonchalant again.

steps.speaker: Corso
steps.content: Whatever you say, boss. Just don't forget your promise. More challenging tasks for me.
Corso has finally agreed to your terms. You breathe a sigh of relief, hoping that this energetic Sinner won't stir more things up anytime soon.
